primitives.name: Temperature Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision A PyTorch-based package of *all* modern post-hoc classification calibration methods in one place — the reference implementation set for the CalArena benchmark.
primitives.assumptions: Model outputs follow a monotonic distortion relative to true posterior probability; the optimal $T$ minimizes cross-entropy against held-out calibration data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overconfident models ($T<1$) become underconfident after scaling; underconfident models ($T>1$) become overconfident. Extreme values can lead to saturated probabilities.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's per-signal row calibration via maximum likelihood estimation on held-out validation sets. Maps to GSI's conformal prediction by interpreting $T$ as a distributionally robust scaling factor.
layer2.telemetry: Measured Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on independent test sets to assess residual miscalibration.

primitives.name: Structured Matrix Scaling (SMS)
primitives.verbatim_quote: It ships: fast accurate temperature scaling, structured matrix scaling (SMS, a regularized matrix scaling), plus integrations of every CalArena-benchmarked method (beta calibration, spline calibration, scaling-binning, netcal's BBQ/ENIR, etc.), and classifier-based Lp calibration-error estimators (a new way to measure ECE without binning artifacts).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$\\mathbf{p}$': 'Vector of un-calibrated model probabilities (dimensionless)', '$\\mathbf{p}^*$': 'Calibrated probability vector (dimensionless)', '$\\mathbf{r}$': 'Observed label frequencies (dimensionless)', '$\\lambda$': 'Regularization strength (inverse squared probability)', '$\\mathbf{M}$': 'Structured transformation matrix (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: The calibrated probabilities lie in the convex hull of the un-calibrated ones, and the regularization enforces smoothness across bins.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $\lambda \rightarrow 0$, SMS reduces to linearly constrained maximum likelihood (binning). When $\lambda \rightarrow \infty$, $\mathbf{p}^* = \mathbf{r}$ (complete rejection).

layer2.mapping: Replicates GSE's state-transition logic where SMS serves as a robust baseline for small-sample signals, replacing ad-hoc binning heuristics with convex optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Average squared deviation of predicted vs. observed frequencies, measured on a separate calibration dataset.

primitives.name: Lp Calibration-Error Estimators
primitives.verbatim_quote: It ships: fast accurate temperature scaling, structured matrix scaling (SMS, a regularized matrix scaling), plus integrations of every CalArena-benchmarked method (beta calibration, spline calibration, scaling-binning, netcal's BBQ/ENIR, etc.), and classifier-based Lp calibration-error estimators (a new way to measure ECE without binning artifacts).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$\\widehat{\\text{ECE}}_p$': 'Estimated expected calibration error (same units as probability)', '$K$': 'Number of bins (dimensionless)', '$\\hat{y}_k$': 'Average predicted probability in bin $k$ (dimensionless)', '$\\bar{y}_k$': 'Observed accuracy in bin $k$ (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: The estimator assumes independent and identically distributed test examples; it converges almost surely to the true ECE as the number of samples grows.
primitives.breakdown_regime: For $p=1$, the estimator is consistent but biased for finite $K$. For $p=2$, it downweights large errors compared to $p=1$, leading to different failure profiles.

layer2.mapping: Serves as the primary telemetry metric in GSE for evaluating calibration methods, replacing naive binned ECE to avoid artifacts from arbitrary bin edges.
layer2.telemetry: Lower values indicate better calibration; used to select the best method on a held-out validation set before deployment.

primitives.name: Beta Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: It ships: fast accurate temperature scaling, structured matrix scaling (SMS, a regularized matrix scaling), plus integrations of every CalArena-benchmarked method (beta calibration, spline calibration, scaling-binning, netcal's BBQ/ENIR, etc.), and classifier-based Lp calibration-error estimators (a new way to measure ECE without binning artifacts).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'$x$': 'Un-calibrated logit (real)', '$f(x)$': 'Calibrated probability (0,1)', '$I^{-1}$': 'Inverse beta CDF (real)', '$a,b$': 'Beta distribution shape parameters (positive reals)'}
primitives.assumptions: The un-calibrated logits follow a beta distribution after binning; the parameters are estimated via maximum likelihood on the calibration set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the calibration set is small or contains rare events, the MLE estimates may be highly uncertain, leading to overfitting and poor generalization.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian updating framework where Beta priors are conjugate to binomial likelihoods, providing a principled way to incorporate prior knowledge about calibration.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive checks using the deviance information criterion (DIC) to assess model fit on the calibration data.

ProbKit-ProbMetrics provides a unified, mathematically rigorous framework for post-hoc calibration that addresses two core challenges in GSE's operational pipeline: small-sample per-signal calibration and regime-shift robustness. Temperature scaling (1 parameter) acts as a safe default for sparse data, while Structured Matrix Scaling (SMS) offers a convex relaxation of binning that avoids artifacts from arbitrary bin edges. The Lp calibration-error estimators eliminate the need for ad hoc binning decisions, yielding a stable empirical metric for model selection. Crucially, the CalArena benchmark establishes that isotonic regression should only be used when sample sizes are large, preventing the 'contaminated-fit' failure mode identified by Garrett. By adopting this library, GSE transitions from heuristic calibration to a principled, data-driven state-transition system where each signal's calibration method is selected based on its own sample size and performance.
